Corticosteroids are the main treatment for blistering in pemphigus and pemphigoid (p.1582). Other immunosuppressants may be added to main- tain disease control and allow a reduction in corticosteroid dosage, and azathioprine is commonly used in this way in pemphigus vulgaris.1 There is limited evidence to suggest that azathioprine may also be effective as monotherapy to induce remission in mild pemphigus.1 Azathioprine has been used similarly in bullous pemphigoid, but there is some disagree- ment about its efficacy,2 and guidelines suggest that it should only be considered if the corticosteroid cannot be reduced to an acceptable dose.3 1.
